prompt: How do I fix list numbering that doesn't continue in Word?
completion:
**Word Numbering that stops in the middle of a document – how to get it to keep going**

Below are the most common reasons a list “stops” and the quick ways to make it continue.  
The steps apply to Word 2016/2019/2021/365; older versions (2007/2010) look slightly different but the concepts are the same.

---

## 1. The list has been split into a *new* list

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| After a page/section break the next paragraph starts with **1** again | Word thinks you started a *different* numbered list | **Right‑click the first item of the new list** → **Continue Numbering** (or choose **Continue from previous list** in the Numbering drop‑down). |

*Tip:*  
If you’re working with a **multilevel list** (Heading 1 → Heading 2 → etc.), the same “Continue Numbering” trick works for every level.

---

## 2. You hit **Enter** *instead* of **Shift+Enter** inside a numbered paragraph

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| The list jumps to 1, 2, 1, 2 because the paragraph is *inside* the numbered line | `Shift+Enter` creates an *in‑line* line break; Word treats it as a new paragraph and starts the list over | **Replace the in‑line break with a real paragraph break** (`Enter`), or press **Ctrl+Shift+L** to apply the numbering style again. |

---

## 3. You copied a list from another document

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| The copied list starts at 1 | Word resets the numbering for each new source | **Right‑click the first item** → **Set List Number Format** → **Continue from previous list**.  If that option is greyed out, make sure the paragraph before the pasted list is still part of the same numbered paragraph (i.e., no section/page break). |

---

## 4. The “Restart numbering” option was accidentally turned on

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| After a couple of items the list restarts at 1 | You clicked **Restart numbering** by accident | **Right‑click the first item after the restart** → **Set List Number Format** → **Continue from previous list**.  Or, choose **Restart at 1** again if you really want to start over. |

---

## 5. Using *multilevel* lists (Headings, etc.) – the list levels don’t chain

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| Level 2 numbers start at 1 after a page break, even though Level 1 kept going | The multilevel list style has *“Restart list numbering at each new page/section”* set | **Modify the list style**:  
1. **Home** ► **Multilevel List** ► **Define New Multilevel List…**  
2. In the dialog, for each level set **“Restart list numbering at”** to **“None”** (or **“Continue previous list”**). |  

---

## 6. A *hidden* “Restart numbering” in the Paragraph style

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| The list keeps restarting on every new paragraph, but you can’t see why | The Paragraph style (e.g., “Heading 1”) has **Restart list numbering** enabled |  
1. **Right‑click** the style in the Styles pane → **Modify**.  
2. Click **Format** ► **Numbering** ► **Set List Number Format**.  
3. Set **“Restart list numbering at”** to **“None”** or **“Continue previous list”**. |  

---

## 7. The numbering “resets” at the start of a new section (Section Break)

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| Each section starts its own numbering series | Word treats each section as a new list |  
1. **File** ► **Options** ► **Advanced** ► **Show document content** ► **Show numbering**  
2. Uncheck **“Restart list numbering at each new page or section”**. |  

---

## 8. Quick “show me the numbering” – the **Show/Hide** trick

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| The numbers look broken or missing | Hidden formatting marks may be messing with the list | Press **Ctrl+Shift+8** (or click **¶** in the Home tab).  This shows paragraph marks, page breaks, and numbering symbols.  If the numbering symbols are hidden, click **Show/Hide** to bring them back. |

---

## 9. “Set List Number Format” – the ultimate control panel

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| You want a custom start number (e.g., “12”) | Word starts from 1 by default |  
1. **Right‑click** the paragraph where the list starts.  
2. Choose **Set List Number Format**.  
3. In the dialog, type the desired **Start at** number and check **“Continue numbering”** or **“Restart”** as needed. |  

---

## 10. When all else fails – reset the list

| What you see | Why it happens | Fix |
|--------------|----------------|-----|
| The list looks completely broken (random numbers, wrong levels) | The list formatting has become corrupted |  
1. **Select the entire list**.  
2. **Right‑click** → **Numbering** ► **None** (or press **Ctrl+Shift+N** to remove formatting).  
3. Re‑apply the numbering style with **Home** ► **Numbering** ► **Continue Numbering** (or pick the desired multilevel list). |

---

## Quick Reference Cheat‑Sheet

| Scenario | One‑liner Fix |
|----------|---------------|
| New page/section breaks restart numbering | `Right‑click first item` → **Continue Numbering** |
| In‑line break (`Shift+Enter`) starts new number | Replace with a real paragraph break (`Enter`) |
| Copied list starts at 1 | `Right‑click first item` → **Set List Number Format** → **Continue from previous list** |
| “Restart numbering” accidentally enabled | Same as above, or use **Define New Multilevel List** and set *“Restart list numbering”* to *None* |
| Section‑break restarts automatically | **File** ► **Options** ► **Advanced** ► Uncheck *Restart list numbering at each new page or section* |
| Want to start at a specific number | `Right‑click` → **Set List Number Format** → **Start at** |

---

### Bottom line

The key to continuous numbering is **“Continue Numbering”**.  
Whenever a list appears to “stop,” it is really Word thinking a *new* list has begun.  Bring it back into the same numbered series with the steps above.  

If you’re still having trouble, let me know the exact Word version and a description of the layout (page/section breaks, headings, etc.) and I’ll give you a more tailored walkthrough. Happy numbering!
